_comment: Pre-registered per-fault target-metric panel (fault_catalog.md §6 realized). For each fault, the Prometheus signal(s) that MUST move if the injection actually took effect. verify_injection.py evaluates these over the baseline vs injection windows and writes a confirmed|borderline|unconfirmed verdict. One target per fault is marked canonical=true (drives the verdict); others are corroborating. Direction: 'increase'|'decrease'. threshold_sigma = min standardized delta over baseline stdev; min_fraction = min share of the injection window past the raw threshold. These are QC gates, NOT the study's modality claims (those live in fault_catalog.md).
_metric_naming: CALIBRATED 2026-07-28 against the live stack. Request-duration metric name differs by service runtime: Go/Node services (catalogue, frontend) expose 'http_request_duration_seconds'; Java/Spring services (cart, orders, payment, user, shipping) expose 'request_duration_seconds'. Prometheus job labels are singular for carts ('cart'). cAdvisor container 'name' labels are 'docker-compose_<svc>_1'; carts=docker-compose_carts_1 (regex '.*carts_1$' excludes carts-db). NOTE: this cAdvisor build exposes NO cfs-throttle metric, so svc_cpu_cap verifies via app latency, not throttle counters.

slow_db_catalogue.name: catalogue_p95_latency
slow_db_catalogue.why: added DB latency inflates catalogue request duration; DB container metrics stay flat (blind spot)

error_storm_catalogue.name: catalogue_5xx_rate
error_storm_catalogue.why: broken DB connections surface as 5xx on catalogue-backed routes

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: throttled service serves requests slower (this cadvisor build has no cfs-throttle metric, so latency is the QC signal)

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_cpu_usage_capped
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: usage pinned at/below the imposed quota

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_memory_limit_dropped
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: the cap is applied: limit drops from host-total (~42GB) to the cap (<=300MB). Reliable for both intensities. (usage/limit ratio is unusable: uncapped baseline limit = host total.) carts working set is ~545MB, so any cap <=300MB necessarily constrains it.

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_oom_kills
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: aggressive cap (160MB, below the working set) forces OOM kills; subtle cap causes GC pressure without necessarily OOMing

dependency_outage_payment.name: payment_cpu_drops
dependency_outage_payment.why: METRICS-WEAK fault (calibrated: payment baseline CPU ~0.004 core drops ~58% to ~0.0018 under pause, smeared by the 1m rate window; may verify BORDERLINE). This aligns with fault_catalog.md: TRACES win this fault (the broken orders->payment edge), not metrics. See orders_5xx note below.

dependency_outage_payment.name: orders_5xx_rate_EXPECTED_BLIND
dependency_outage_payment.why: CALIBRATION FINDING: stays ~0. docker pause FREEZES payment, so orders' HTTP call HANGS (blocked socket read) rather than fail-fast - the request never completes with an error status inside the window. A frozen dependency is metrics/logs-INVISIBLE while the kernel sees orders threads blocked in read() on the payment socket. This is a concrete instance of the study's kernel-wins thesis; kept as documentation, not a verification gate.

queue_backlog.name: queue_master_cpu_drops
queue_backlog.why: calibrated: queue-master baseline CPU ~0.008 core drops ~77% to ~0.0019 under pause (1m-rate-smeared). METRICS-WEAK silent-failure fault: orders keep succeeding, no error anywhere; the real signal is the KERNEL (queue-master cgroup goes quiet while rabbitmq keeps taking inbound) - matches fault_catalog.md's kernel-wins prediction.

noisy_neighbor.name: neighbor_cpu_active
noisy_neighbor.why: confirms the stress container is actually running at its cap. NOTE: this verifies the fault FIRED, not that services were affected - noisy_neighbor's premise is that service KPIs stay within normal variance (checked separately in calibration).

anomaly_net.name: host_net_throughput_drop
anomaly_net.why: tbf shaping + netem loss reduce effective throughput (corroborate with probe latency)
